more.good_when: The README's case "Adding a work with `overnight` starts the waiting works again too" has its own test: works left pending by a runner that stopped, then a new work added, and the waiting works run, the one that was running first, then the new one. Today every test that adds a work adds it while a runner already runs, so a maintainer who made the add start the runner only where no work waits would pass every test and coverage, while the works left after a restart sit until the user thinks to run `overnight` alone.

The case of a work added just as the runner ends checks the runner through what its callers use, with no stand-in for `queue.pending` inside `queue.run`. Today test_a_work_added_just_as_the_runner_ends_still_runs replaces `queue.pending` by monkeypatch, so a maintainer who changes how `run` looks for the works, with the behavior kept, sees that test fail, and one who keeps the call but breaks the lock order may see it still pass.

The case of a work added while another runs asserts the whole result of the command, as the other cases of the command do: exit 0, nothing on stderr, and the two lines on stdout. Today test_a_work_added_while_another_runs_waits_in_the_queue_after_it checks stdout only, so the add path could exit non-zero or write on stderr, which Claude Code shows the user as a failure, with every test passing.
